interest: Japan's foreign advisers Henry W. Kinney and Thomas Baty, and Baty's 70th birthday.
overview: State Department decimal file 894.01A (covering December 1937 to September 1939) documents the employment, activities, and celebrations surrounding foreign advisers attached to the Japanese Government, specifically the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Gaimusho). The file opens with a December 1937 consular despatch from Harbin reporting that the Tokyo Foreign Office had re-engaged American publicist Henry W. Kinney, formerly the chief English-language publicity agent of the South Manchuria Railway Company, for propaganda work in North China and Shanghai. The remainder and primary bulk of the file details efforts by Japanese civic organizer Sakae Katayama to celebrate the seventieth birthday of Dr. Thomas Baty, an eminent British jurist who had served as legal adviser to the Gaimusho since 1916. Katayama sent petitions and follow-up solicitations to President Franklin D. Roosevelt and Secretary of State Cordell Hull, enclosing biographical pamphlets, Japanese prospectuses with lists of prominent signatories, and a Tokyo Asahi newspaper clipping describing Baty's nationwide celebration and requesting tributes for a souvenir album. Internal State Department correspondence reveals Washington's decision to decline official felicitations in accordance with established policy, instructing Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo to politely decline the request and later filing Katayama's follow-up letters without action.
